# swayosd

On-screen display for volume and brightness, and the commands the keys run.

Styled in the Viewport CAD look (`style.css`): 0px opaque `vp_bar`, 1px `vp_cyan` 45% border, Terminess 14px bold tabular label, `vp_cyan` icon (`vp_dim` when muted) and a solid `vp_cyan` level bar over an 8px ruler-ticked trough. `osd-brightness` keeps two verb pairs: `up`/`down` (keys) show the OSD, while `bup`/`bdown` (waybar `BRI` scroll) call `brightnessctl` directly in 1% steps.

## Reference

<!-- generated by tools/docs: reference -->
**Packages** (`swayosd/packages`): `swayosd`, `brightnessctl`

**Linked into your home** (stow, `install.sh --link`):

- `~/.config/swayosd/colors.css`
- `~/.config/swayosd/style.css`
- `~/.config/systemd/user/swayosd.service`
- `~/.local/bin/osd-brightness`
- `~/.local/bin/osd-volume`

**Rendered from the palette** (`theme`):

- `swayosd/.config/swayosd/colors.css.tmpl` → `swayosd/.config/swayosd/colors.css`: `name`, `slug`, `vp_bar`, `vp_cyan`, `vp_dim`, `vp_text`

**User units** (enabled by `install.sh --units`): `swayosd.service`

**`setup.sh`** (run by `install.sh --setup`): your user in the video group, so the brightness keys (swayosd) and the bar's brightness scroll (waybar) can write the backlight. Both run as systemd user units, outside the logind session, so logind's SetBrightness (brightnessctl's fallback without write access) refuses them; the backlight's brightness file is root:video and group-writable. Applies from the next login.

**`reload.sh`** (run by `theme set`): restart swayosd.service, which reads its colors at startup. try-restart leaves a stopped unit alone (a bar hidden with its toggle stays hidden).
